title: Workspaces, multiple environments, and where Terragrunt fits

videos.script: Ana has one network for the shop, and now she needs two. One where she can break things, and one that customers use. {{two}} The code should be the same. Only the values differ: the address range, how many zones, how big things are. {{values}} So she keeps one configuration and swaps the file of values. The plan that comes back does not build a second network. It replaces the first one. {{replace}} That is where this lesson starts. Two environments need two states, and there are three common ways to keep them apart. {{three}} Workspaces switch the state behind one directory. You will watch that go wrong, with a command that looks right and plans to destroy production. {{workspace}} Separate directories put the environment in the path, at the cost of copied files. {{directories}} And Terragrunt writes those copies for you, then runs Terraform in each one, in order. {{terragrunt}} By the end you can choose between the three, and say what each one protects you from, and what it does not. {{choose}}
